parameters.pressure: vacuumed to 5−7 Pa, filled with argon to about 60 kPa for melting, argon pressure increased to about 100 kPa during melting

evidence.quote: The ingots were melted in a laboratory arc furnace with a nonconsumable tungsten electrode on a water-cooled copper hearth. The furnace was vacuumed to 5−7 Pa, purged with argon of grade A (impurities of 0.01 wt.% N2, 0.003 wt.% O2, 3·10−5 kg/m3 moisture), and filled with argon to reach about 60 kPa for melting. During the melting, the argon pressure increased to about 100 kPa.

attributes.location: alloys with 12 at.% Nb or Ta

evidence.quote: Only do alloys with 12 at.% Nb or Ta contain superfine bright grains, which can be considered depending on their composition and the phase ratio [10, 11] as the stabilized β phase.
The (111) reflection typical of the β0 phase of CsCl type was not observed at 2θ ≈ 48.2°.
The microstructure of the alloys testifies that grains of the high-temperature phase decomposed during cooling are coarse (Figs. 2 and 3).
All alloys show a superfine lamellar structure of decomposition β → α → α + γ → α2 + γ with submicron-thickness lamellas visible at large magnifications (major gray component).
Niobium and tantalum doping leads to dendritic segregation, which can be seen from light and dark layers enriched with heavy or light components, respectively.
The fracture patterns revealed that the material demonstrated a transcrystalline failure mechanism (Fig. 8 a). The cracks propagating within individual grains show ribbon-like fracture (Fig. 8 b)
